{"content": "1|## Why custom parsers?
2|
3|Before choosing custom parsers, I evaluated:
4|
5|- ~~`clang++ -ast-dump=json`~~
6|  - Even when only parsing the AST, `clang` requires valid input. Unfortunately,
7|    the current C++ headers provided by OpenFX are broken, so I would have to
8|    inject dummy code to make it work, which feels very hacky.
9|  - Even with an AST, it would be filled with noise, and I would still have to
10|    understand its structure to extract the information I need.
11|- ~~`npm:tree-sitter`~~
12|  - Its installation requires running build scripts. Given the JavaScript
13|    ecosystem's supply-chain security issues, I do not like that idea.
14|  - Although I have not verified it myself, it does not appear to provide
15|    TypeScript types for its output, so I would still have to understand the
16|    output structure.
17|
18|Instead, I defined the types I need, wrote tests to validate them, chose a
19|parser library that works in plain JavaScript, and let LLMs handle the rest.
20|
21|Because the problem is well-defined, the code runs only occasionally, is never
22|exposed to users, and is sandboxed within Deno, I consider this a good use case
23|for vibe coding. In other words, I did not look into the generated code here.
